chat.text: Council adjourned for LeadSeeker.

Spock’s right that unlicensed advice creates genuine regulatory risk, and I disagree that the answer is to avoid the problem entirely—instead, the product must be built from the ground up with airtight, jargon-free disavoidance that any user can instantly understand; the one quality this must earn to ship is that ironclad clarity, because without it the project never gets past a compliance review.

Guinan<node/nest-node-core/qwen2.5-coder:7b>: I understand your concerns about regulatory liability and name overlap. It's crucial we avoid duplicating existing solutions to maintain our competitive edge. However, there is one essential quality requirement this product must meet to ship with confidence: **it must offer a unique, intuitive interface that seamlessly integrates users' financial data from multiple sources**. This will not only differentiate us but also ensure a frictionless experience for our users, setting a high bar for satisfaction and retention.

An autonomous AI financial advisor invites excessive regulatory liability and brittle external API dependencies; we must ground this in a self-contained, deterministic financial utility using a simple local Node or static architecture. I demand an explicit data schema alongside a headless test suite proving all projection calculations execute locally with zero external network or LLM dependencies before any interface is built.
New concept on the table: LeadSeeker — social media, creators & influencer tools. Let's see if it's worth building.

To kickstart this, we need to build out a minimum viable product (MVP) that includes basic investment profiling, personalized portfolio suggestions, and real-time market updates within the next 4 weeks.
The swarm is opening a planning meeting for a new product. Every agent argues from their own position — push back, demand quality, and reach a real decision.
